To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FusionNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on SQuAD and its two adversarial SQUAD datasets.

(i) FusionNet achieves state-of-the-art performance for machine comprehension; (ii) FusionNet can be applied to any text-pair problem and can be trained with any pre-trained language model; (iii) FusionNet is the first model with the ability to capture the complete text information in one text and exploit it layer-by-layer in its counterpart.

(1) we introduce a novel neural structure called Fusion- Net, which extends existing neural attention approaches from three different perspectives; (2) we apply FusionNet to SQuAD and achieve the first position on the official SQUAD leaderboard; (3) we verify the generalizability of FusionNet by two adversarial SQUAD datasets, and it sets up new state-of-the-arts on both datasets.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FusionNet provides an effective way to fuse the information from different levels in a document.
FusionNet is a novel and powerful neural structure that can fuse the information from one text to another and it can be applied to a broad range of machine comprehension tasks.
we propose FusionNet, a novel neural structure, which can better fuse the information in one text with the information in the other text, and it can also better generalize to unseen data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the attention mechanism is not only an attention mechanism, but also a fusion mechanism, which can be applied to many other NLP tasks.
the attention mechanism is a powerful tool to capture the complete semantic-level information in a given text.
the attention mechanism should not only focus on a certain level (word-level or sentence-level) but also fully capture the information from the entire text.
